summary: Weekly co-sell pipeline review: top deals, mutual plays, ask/commitments. Key focus on 3 prioritized accounts, technical benchmark for private deployment options, commercial alignment on partner discount and win-splits, and next steps to enable a joint outreach and exec intro.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-08 14:00 PST | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Maya Patel, Leo Grant, Ana Morales (Redwood); Sarah Nguyen, Omar Ruiz, Priya Rao (Verdant)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, um we just wanted to run through the co-sell pipeline and make sure we're aligned on next steps. I see Sarah, Omar, Priya, thanks for making time.
[00:12] Sarah: Yeah thanks Maya, excited to go through — we've got a few deals where Redwood looks like a good fit.
[00:18] Leo: quick note on my side, I'm Leo from Redwood, SE, I'll cover the benchmark ask and tech constraints. Apologies in advance if audio is rough, connection is a bit spotty on my end.
[00:27] Omar: No worries, we can hear you.
[00:30] Maya: Cool. First slide, high level — we prioritized three accounts: Evergreen Health, AgroMax, and FinSight. Sarah, you had updated the probability and timing?
[00:40] Sarah: yep. Evergreen Health — our internal sponsor is a CPO, timing Q1-Q2 2027, estimated ARR $450k; AgroMax looks like a pilot for their field ops automation, Q1 2027, $120k ARR potential; FinSight is a larger chase, decision timeline longer, maybe Q2-Q3 2027 and $1.2M ARR if we land it. Those are our top 3.
[01:05] Maya: great. For Evergreen Health we recommended Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) because of PHI concerns, but we flagged Redwood Private as an option if they require on-prem or air-gapped. Priya, from a solutions perspective, is the PHI constraint blocking hosted?
[01:22] Priya: they want control over data residency and audit logs, and their legal team pushes for customer-managed keys. Hosted with SaaS KMS isn't a no-go, but they'd prefer VPC or private control plane. So private deployment looks more aligned.
[01:35] Leo: got it. Technical note — our Private stack supports customer-managed KMS (we call out HSM integrations) and per-tenant audit logs; latency tends to be a hair higher than hosted but consistent. We ran similar deployment for Melody Health last quarter.
[01:50] Omar: what's the cost delta roughly between hosted vs dedicated vs private? this is always what our execs ask.
[01:57] Maya: short answer, hosted is lowest up-front, dedicated is middle (reserved commit reduces per-token), private has platform/license + infra. For Evergreen if they need private we should expect a platform fee and longer procurement. For co-sell how does Verdant want to position margin?
[02:14] Sarah: we typically go for a 15% partner margin for SaaS outcomes, but for strategic logos we're flexible to 20%. We need clarity on Redwood's recommended partner discount so we can align externally.
[02:27] Maya: we can offer a partner discount on committed Dedicated deals and a referral fee for hosted. I'll share the partner pricing sheet.
[02:34] Ana: also want to flag partner enablement — we can do a 1:1 onboarding workshop and joint technical onboarding for the first 2 deals.
[02:41] Priya: perfect, that helps. Next, AgroMax — they're more cost-sensitive, latency requirements low, but footprint is large, hundreds of field devices. They might prefer quantized models to reduce compute.
[02:55] Leo: for edge/quantized workloads we can suggest Redwood Optimize recommendations and lighter-weight model variants; we also have batching strategies to keep per-token cost down. Will want to test accuracy regressions with their prompts.
[03:10] Sarah: can Redwood run a short benchmark? they'll want a POC for AgroMax with a week-long pilot.
[03:15] Leo: yes, we can. Plan would be: get test dataset + sample prompts, spin up a dedicated test environment (hosted or private depending on their data rules), run throughput/latency/cost profiling, then share results. Should be 2 weeks end-to-end but initial numbers in 3-5 days.
[03:29] Maya: let's commit to a benchmark plan. Leo, you'll own it with Priya as point on the Verdant side.
[03:35] Leo: noted.
[03:37] Omar: for FinSight, it's complicated — they already evaluate HelixTech and Meridian, and there's mention of using Bedrock in their infra. How do we compete on reliability and cost?
[03:48] Maya: main plays: 1) show performance SLOs and predictable unit economics via Dedicated; 2) show reliability/fallbacks and multi-variant routing; 3) partner-led enterprise support and runbooks. We should prepare a competitive battlecard.
[04:03] Sarah: yes, FinSight is security-first, they'll want SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, audit trails. Do we have SOC2 in our docs?
[04:12] Maya: Redwood is SOC2 Type II compliant, we have the cert and security pack. I'll share the package. Also we can demo SAML/SSO and RBAC in the console.
[04:21] Priya: note that FinSight asks about private deployments and colocation in their EU region. Data residency is a big checkbox.
[04:28] Leo: our private offering supports region placement; we recently deployed to an EU VPC for a customer — some kernel tuning required but it's supported. We'll want to capture exact residency requirements.
[04:40] Sarah: cool. On commercial splits — do you have a standard co-sell agreement or should Verdant propose a contract?
[04:48] Ana: we have a partner co-sell template we can share, includes commission tiers, partner discounts, and lead registration. I'll attach to the deck.
[04:56] Omar: onboarding timeline question: for a Dedicated commit, how long from signed to live?
[05:02] Maya: depends on capacity and config; typical is 4-8 weeks for a dedicated pool and integrations, faster for hosted. For private it can be 8-12 weeks including network/security setup.
[05:12] Priya: that's in line with expectations. For Evergreen, procurement timeline might push to Q2 so the 8-12 week schedule still works.
[05:20] Leo: technical risk items — model quantization impact on accuracy for AgroMax, KV cache behavior for long-context FinSight prompts, and network egress costs for multi-region private deployment. We'll detail these in the benchmark.
[05:36] Sarah: can Redwood provide reference customers with similar setups? we found that helps close.
[05:40] Maya: yes, Melody Health (PHI), Vertex Farming (edge/quantized), and Lumina Finance (private EU) are good references. I'll pull contactable refs in the pack.
[05:50] Omar: competition again — HelixTech pitches lower latency on their custom runtime, Meridian pitches integrated data platform. How do we position Redwood?
[05:59] Maya: we lean into consistent production economics, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, and predictable rollouts — and partner enablement for go-to-market. We also emphasize observability and rollback/fallback policies for production reliability.
[06:12] Priya: one nit — does Redwood support function/tool calling or structured outputs? FinSight uses structured parsers heavily.
[06:19] Leo: yes, we support function-calling primitives and structured output enforcement; we also have eval tooling to validate regression on prompts.
[06:26] Sarah: ok great. Let's capture blockers: 1) commercial clarity on partner discount and win-split, 2) benchmark plan + timeline, 3) security docs and references, 4) target account list and intro contacts.
[06:40] Maya: agree. We'll add those as action items.
[06:43] Omar: one more — for AgroMax's field devices, they'd prefer a local inference footprint to minimize egress; is Redwood optimizing for quantized local runtimes?
[06:53] Leo: we don't ship a lightweight device runtime as a product, but we can help advise model quantization and edge packaging partners; Redwood Optimize recommendations plus partner integrations are the path there. Might be a partner co-sell with an edge vendor.
[07:07] Priya: fair.
[07:09] Sarah: ok recap and next steps please.
[07:11] Maya: recap: Maya to send joint deck/partner pricing + co-sell template + SOC2 pack by 2026-12-12; Leo to run benchmark plan for AgroMax and share test plan by 2026-12-13; Sarah to confirm target account contacts by 2026-12-10; schedule exec intro 2026-12-16. Any objections?
[07:28] Omar: none from me.
[07:29] Priya: all good.
[07:30] Leo: I'll follow up with a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff once Priya shares the dataset.
[07:35] Maya: awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next week if necessary.
[07:40] [meeting closed]
notes: Verdant prioritized Evergreen Health, AgroMax, and FinSight
Private deployment likely needed for PHI use-case (Evergreen)
Benchmark required for AgroMax (quantized workload) - Leo to lead
Commercial clarity needed on partner discount and win-split
